question: The ESF+ is the main instrument through which the European Union invests in people and supports the implementation of the European Pillar of Social Rights. The EUR 142.7billion budget for the period 2021-2027 must continue to make a significant contribution to EU policies on employment, society, education and skills, including structural reforms in these areas. Can the Commission say: 1.
What are the methods and mechanisms for monitoring the use of the budget?
What measures does the Commission take to ensure that the funds are used reasonably and for the purposes of the Fund?
How does the Commission ensure that the funds are not used for reasons and purposes other than the areas mentioned above?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.1.2026) The use of the European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) is monitored through the monitoring committees (Articles 11 and 38, Regulation (EU) 2021/1060)1, annual review meetings between the Commission and Member States (Article 41, Regulation (EU) 2021/1060) and regular reporting on implementation and performance.

Additionally, the Commission assesses performance through ongoing monitoring and the mid-term review (Article 18, Regulation (EU) 2021/1060). When non-compliance is detected, the Commission may interrupt payment deadlines, suspend payments and apply financial corrections.

Members States may only use ESF+ resources to support the specific objective set out in the ESF+ Regulation (Article 4, Regulation (EU) 2021/10572). To ensure funds are used for the designated purposes, programmes are agreed between the Commission and the Member States before being approved by the Commission.

The programmes have to address country-specific recommendations stemming from the European Semester work while complying with horizontal principles and safeguards, in particular the fulfilment of enabling conditions (Articles 9 and 15, Regulation (EU) 2021/1060). Enabling conditions ensure that operations are in line with the relevant policy strategies and meet the conditions set out in the legal framework.
